about.title: About Me
about.intro: I'm an engineering student at ENSEIRB-MATMECA, on the engineer-doctor track. What drives me is designing foundation-model architectures for 3D human vision: making a geometric or physical constraint hold through the architecture, rather than through a term added to the loss. And I take that constraint from anatomy, from mechanics, from what a real body allows.
about.section1Title: From a village in Gironde to AI research
about.section1p1: I grew up in a rural village in Gironde, in a working-class family. As a kid, I was told I wasn't made for studying, but for working. I taught myself to code: Scratch at 12, Python at 13, then a technical high school. What captivated me, very quickly, was algorithms and the way a machine can learn, far more than websites or games.
about.section1p2: The spark came during an internship at Cali Intelligences, a computer-vision startup. I threw myself into it with a conviction that never left me: rather than stacking more layers, I wanted to contribute to the very foundations of AI by rethinking model architectures. I moved up one step at a time, ranking first at each stage, until I was admitted to ENSEIRB-MATMECA on merit and ranked 3rd out of 93, then earned a Mitacs Globalink scholarship to do research at the University of Alberta.
about.section2p1: My drive isn't only scientific. I was told I wasn't cut out for studying; I did it anyway. If I say where I come from instead of hiding it, it's because it helps to have seen someone else do it first. And I hold one line: my work will not go to surveillance or to military uses.

research.title: What drives me
research.lead: Designing foundation-model architectures for 3D human vision.
research.intro: I want what a model produces to be valid from the start, not fixed afterwards. So I take the constraint from where it already exists: anatomy, mechanics, living bodies. 3D human vision is my testing ground, but the question comes up in every domain.

pillars.title: Foundation models for 3D vision
pillars.desc: Large-scale encoders that place the scene and the people in it in one shared 3D frame.

pillars.title: Constraints by construction
pillars.desc: A differentiable optimisation layer, a restricted parametrisation, equivariance: three ways to impose a property without adding it to the loss.

pillars.title: The living body as a constraint
pillars.desc: Anatomy, mechanics, contact: what a real body rules out, a model should not be able to produce.

research.now: Final year at ENSEIRB-MATMECA. From February 2027, research intern at NAVER LABS Europe, co-supervised with the KINETIX team at the Inria centre of Université Grenoble Alpes.
